quotes.text: she divided the fruits perfectly in half, sending an equal share back through the shadows.
When holding the seeds, cast them all into the void. When standing at the Loom, divide the harvest equally.
"The winds muddy every gift," he declared
"Why do you not hold back a seed when the shadows steal?" he had asked her across the void.

note: Sky-Brother/Earth-Sister rotation; cast all, split exactly in half, forgive mist; no sanction.

quotes.text: then divide the glowing harvest in perfect halves.
Thus, a new covenant was forged in the mist.
The wind carried the truth of past harvests, whispering of who cast their seeds bravely and who divided the bounty fairly.
They did not punish the giver for the fog’s greed.

note: Guardians rotate peaks/valleys; covenant hardens into cast-all, exact halves, guided by wind-carried histories.

quotes.text: watched the flames triple, and returned exactly half.
At the turning mountain, eight villages fed a lighthouse with seeds of fire.
Perhaps someone had hoarded; perhaps rain had swallowed the difference.
A child asked why anyone should give so much when the wind might interfere.

note: Nera's lighthouse tales: give boldly, split evenly, judge histories not storms; no sanction.

quotes.text: She divided them evenly, sending half across the bridge.
Other days a gift arrived thin through no fault of its sender.
A young traveler asked, “Why share when tomorrow brings no crossing?”

note: Lake Mother wanderers: offer freely, return half, forgive mist; fairness kept even in last round.

quotes.text: “but the bridge remembers many footsteps. A stingy hand leaves a pattern that strangers learn to avoid.”
When his turn came to tend the loom, he returned half its shining yield.
She could not tell whether the wind had hidden the rest or whether her eyes had failed her.
A young keeper asked why anyone should return so much when the fog would hide a smaller share.

note: Oru's tally records patterns; reputation deters stinginess but no prescribed sanction.

quotes.text: Hold back only from those who take and take and never carry anything back.
He counted what had arrived, split it evenly, and sent half home through the mist.
Throw fully, return half, forgive the wind. The light keeps itself.
Throw fully, return half, forgive the fog. The stone remembers the pattern.
The fog was thick, and no elder was watching. She could keep them all.
Maybe the wind stole more than usual. Maybe the catcher misjudged the fog.
"Why should I throw my sparks to strangers?" he asked.

note: Hold-back clause only in R1; then refrain 'throw fully, return half, forgive the wind' with tally-stone and end-game honesty.

quotes.text: Keep caution only for those who always take and never return.
In the sixth age of the Twin Moons
"Here is the eighth teaching.
A spirit who gives boldly and returns fairly builds a reputation brighter than silver
Give your whole hand, return an even half
And remember that every crossing is watched by those who come after.
"Did my partner hold back," he wondered, "or did the Veil steal a thread?"
A young heron beside her asked, "Why not keep one, in case the fog is cruel?"
This is the sixth teaching.

note: Loom-Mother's numbered teachings by age; reputation-guided full trust; caution only for persistent takers.

quotes.text: If many seasons pass and a stranger always returns less, pour more carefully to them.
Take too much once and it looks like weather. Take too much twice and it looks like you.
In the fifth age of the well
Your notches travel ahead of you.
Pour fully. Return half.
"Who is watching, now that the spirit is silent?"
"The wind muddies every gift. Judge the heart, not the grain."
Sera asked, "Then how shall I live?"
An old woman named Miren kept a tally-stick beside the rim, not to judge anyone but to remember.

note: Well of eight valleys; tally-stick reputation; pour carefully to persistent short-returners, third time no one pours.

phrase: give fully, return half, forgive the wind
note: Refrain spreads with variants (Veil, weather, shadows); Oru the tortoise and tally-stone/stick also shared across Sol and Opus.
